title: Detection of RHIM-protein oligomeric complex formation in HEK293T cells
author: Mishra, Dey, et al.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysates to separate fractions
steps.instruction: After stopping the DSP crosslinking reaction, centrifuge the whole‑cell lysates at 6000 × g for 15–20 min at 4 °C to pellet insoluble material and retain the supernatant.

steps.title: Collect soluble supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant (soluble fraction) into a fresh microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Prepare soluble lysate for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Divide the collected supernatant into two equal 125 µL aliquots; add 4X sample buffer containing β‑mercaptoethanol (BME) to one aliquot and 4X sample buffer without BME to the other.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 125 µL of supernatant into tube A
Aliquot 125 µL of supernatant into tube B
Add 4X sample buffer with BME to tube A
Add 4X sample buffer without BME to tube B

steps.title: Resuspend insoluble pellet
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL NP‑40‑HEPES lysis buffer (without DSP) to the pellet and vortex or pipette to dissolve.

steps.title: Prepare insoluble lysate for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Divide the dissolved pellet into two equal 125 µL aliquots; add 4X sample buffer with BME to one and 4X sample buffer without BME to the other.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 125 µL of dissolved pellet into tube C
Aliquot 125 µL of dissolved pellet into tube D
Add 4X sample buffer with BME to tube C
Add 4X sample buffer without BME to tube D

steps.title: Boil samples to denature
steps.instruction: Heat all prepared samples at 95 °C for 5–10 min.

description: Regulated inflammatory cell death activation in response to pathogenic infections or endogenous triggers is an innate host defense mechanism.2,3,4 Receptor-interacting serine/threonine protein (RIP) kinase 1 (RIPK1), RIPK3, Toll/IL-1 receptor domain-containing adapter protein-inducing IFN-β (TRIF), and Z-nucleic acid binding protein 1 (ZBP1) are cell death signaling proteins that harbor conserved protein motifs called RIP Homotypic interaction motifs (RHIM).5,6 RHIMs mediate homotypic protein-protein interactions and oligomerization of the cell death proteins. The core tetrad residues (I/V-Q-I/V/L/C-G) in RHIMs are critical for stacking β-sheet structures to form higher-order amyloid-like signaling complexes, essential for cell death and inflammatory signaling.6,7,8 Several viruses encode viral RHIM proteins that mimic host RHIMs and modulate host cell death.9,10,11 Here, we describe a protocol for detecting RHIM-mediated complex formation of host/viral RHIM proteins. The protocol involves DSP-mediated crosslinking to preserve the oligomeric complexes. DSP (dithiobis(succinimidylpropionate)) is a membrane-permeable crosslinking reagent that reacts with the primary amines of interacting proteins to crosslink them. The crosslinked complexes can be decoupled with reducing agents due to an intrinsic disulfide bond in the spacer arm of DSP (Figure 1). This protocol will be useful for the quick and easy detection of RHIM-mediated complex formation. It will further provide a better understanding of RHIM-RHIM interaction-mediated host cell death signaling and the crosstalk between host and viral RHIM proteins. Using this protocol, we recently demonstrated that the viral RHIM (CoV-RHIM-1) in SARS-CoV-2 Nsp13 promotes higher order complex formation of host RHIM proteins - ZBP1 and RIPK3, when co-expressed in HEK-293T cells, to promote cell death.1Figure 1Mechanism of action for DSP-mediated crosslinking of interacting RHIM proteinsDSP (Dithiobis (succinimidyl propionate)) rea
